issues.description: Reading the whole compiled script into the RPC response just to enable a download is the wrong shape.
issues.detail: The backend already wrote the file to disk and returns its path. Stuffing the full file contents into every compile response wastes memory and bandwidth on a payload that's only sometimes used. Add a download RPC that reads the file on demand, or have the frontend fetch the path. Don't bloat the compile response for one button.

issues.description: open() without encoding and without error handling on a path that just came back from compile.
issues.detail: If compile_pipeline succeeded but the script file is missing, unreadable, or non-utf8 on the user's locale, this throws and the entire compile_notebook RPC fails after the real work succeeded. Wrap it, specify encoding='utf-8', or skip reading entirely. The RPC swallowing a post-success IOError as a compile failure is a bad user experience.

issues.description: Download button has no disabled/empty-content guard in the rendered output.
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick checks compiledContent, but the icon renders unconditionally in the success branch. If compiledContent is missing (older backend, partial response), the user clicks and nothing happens with no feedback. Either gate rendering on compiledContent or show a disabled state. Silent no-op clicks are hostile.

issues.description: Duplicate state: compiledPath and compiledContent both flow through props when one would do.
issues.detail: compiledPath is used only to derive the filename via split('/').pop(). The backend could return just a filename plus content, or the frontend could keep the path alone and fetch content on click. Carrying both through DeployProgressState, DeploysProgress, DeployProgress, and Commands is the kind of prop-drilling that the maintainer six years from now will curse.

issues.description: GetAppIcon used as a click target instead of an actual button.
issues.detail: It's an SVG icon with onClick and a title attr. No keyboard handler, no role, no focus ring, not a button. The existing 'Done' link next to it is an anchor for a reason. Wrap in IconButton or an <a download> with an object URL stored in state. Match the surrounding code's voice.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The feature is fine; the shape is wrong. Sending the entire compiled script in every compile_notebook RPC response just so a button can save a blob is bloat — add a dedicated download RPC or read on demand. The backend open() has no encoding and no error handling, so a post-success read failure poisons the whole compile result. The frontend renders the download icon without gating on compiledContent and uses an SVG as a click target instead of a real button. Two pieces of duplicated path/content state get drilled through four files when one would do. Good taste here is eliminating the special case: one path, fetched when clicked.
